theme: 3 terms on properties: how a type keeps and works out values

terms.definition: A variable or constant inside a type that keeps its own value.
terms.example: Make `name` a stored property, so each user keeps their own name.

terms.definition: A property that does not keep a value and works out its result each time you read it.
terms.example: Make `total` a computed property, so it always matches the price and quantity.

terms.definition: Code that runs right before or after a property changes its value.
terms.example: Add a property observer, so the label updates when the score changes.

video.title: Stored, Computed & Property Observer | iOS Daily English Day 12
video.description:
Learn to talk about Swift properties: Stored Property, Computed Property and Property Observer, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Stored Property - A variable or constant inside a type that keeps its own value.
Computed Property - A property that does not keep a value and works out its result each time you read it.
Property Observer - Code that runs right before or after a property changes its value.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Day 12 of the iOS Daily English series: 3 terms a day, from Swift basics to advanced iOS.

landscape.description:
Explain Stored Property, Computed Property and Property Observer in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
저장 프로퍼티, 계산 프로퍼티, 프로퍼티 옵저버 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Stored Property - A variable or constant inside a type that keeps its own value.
한국어: 값을 직접 저장하는 타입 안의 변수 또는 상수

Computed Property - A property that does not keep a value and works out its result each time you read it.
한국어: 값을 저장하지 않고 읽을 때마다 결과를 계산하는 프로퍼티

Property Observer - Code that runs right before or after a property changes its value.
한국어: 프로퍼티 값이 바뀌기 직전이나 직후에 실행되는 코드

dialogue.title: The cart total

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I made `qty` a stored property in my `Cart` type.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. A stored property keeps its own value.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Now I need `total`. Should I save it too?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No, make it a computed property. It works out `qty * 10` each time.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So a computed property never gets out of date?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. Change `qty`, and `total` is always correct.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I also want a message when `qty` changes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Add a property observer. Use `didSet` after the value changes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I wrote `willSet` first, but it runs before the change.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, use `didSet`. A property observer can run before or after.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Great. Stored, computed, and observer, all in one type.
Make `name` a stored property, so each user keeps theirs.
